reasoning: Resolve every fixed arrow chain to an undecided cell or the outside sink. Any cycle consisting only of fixed arrows invalidates the entire grid because every starting cell must escape. Each undecided cell then has four labeled choices of destination in the compressed graph; choices returning to itself are invalid. A valid replacement is exactly a directed spanning tree oriented toward the outside sink, with parallel choices counted separately. Construct the outgoing Laplacian minor and use the directed matrix-tree theorem; its determinant modulo the prime counts all valid choices. Modular Gaussian elimination handles row swaps and zero pivots, and an empty determinant is one when all fixed chains escape.
